From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@fastretail.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent missing tokens in completions

Hi Soojin / Alex,

We're seeing intermittent truncation / missing tokens on completions from the redwood-hosted endpoint for our product catalog summarization job. Example: a 1,200-token prompt returns a completion that abruptly ends mid-sentence (no stop token, no error). This has happened ~5 times in the last 24 hours across different model variants (rwd-base-30b, rwd-opt-13b).

I attached a screenshot and the curl request we used. We tried bumping max_tokens and got the same cut-off. Session id in the header is x-session: fr-20260914-97b.

Impact: downstream UI shows an incomplete description for ~0.3% of runs. Not a hard outage but want to get ahead of it. Can you confirm if this is on your side or if we need to change how we call the API?

Attachments: screencap_missing_tokens_0914.png, curl_run_0914.txt

Thanks,
Lydia

Initial ask: can you confirm the exact model name in the API call (payload/model) and whether you were using streaming or non-streaming output for these runs? Also, can you share one raw output (the truncated text) so we can compare tokenization?

Plan: Alex will try to reproduce against the same model and sequence length, and Karhtik is looped in to check runtime logs for any early termination / worker-side cancellations. We'll aim to update you within 24–48 hours.

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent missing tokens in completions

Hi Lydia — quick update from triage (I'm sending the technical details here so your engineers can follow).

What we did:
- Pulled the example curl you attached and replayed it against the same model variants and sequence lengths you listed.
- Ran 250 test invocations matching the prompt/headers (non-streaming).
- Checked server-side logs for the session id you provided (fr-20260914-97b) and surrounding times.

Findings:
- We were unable to reproduce the abrupt truncation in any of our replays. All runs completed with expected token counts.
- The runtime logs show normal full-token emission for the request windows in question; no worker crash, no OOM, no preemptions. See snippet attached (redwood_console_run_abc123.txt).
- We did observe that your original curl sets Content-Length explicitly and includes a client-side token filter that may truncate at a local buffer boundary. We also saw a pattern where the client-side SDK flags a local timeout at ~8s and then displays the partial body to the UI — that matches the symptom you described.

Conclusion (interim): No evidence of server-side truncation. Most likely explanation is client-side/SDK timeout or local proxy that cuts the response before the client finishes streaming. To help rule this out: can you try a streaming call and capture the full response bytes (or rerun without explicit Content-Length / with a longer client timeout)?

Links: https://console.redwood.ai/runs/abc123 (console run with log snippets).

If you still see truncation after the above, send one raw truncated payload (exact bytes) and we'll escalate to infra for deeper packet-level traces.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@fastretail.com>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent missing tokens in completions — Closure

Hi Lydia,

Thanks for working through the repro. Per Alex's triage and our replay tests, we couldn't reproduce truncation from the Redwood side and we found no runtime anomalies tied to your session ids. The most likely cause appears to be client-side: either an SDK/proxy timeout or an intermediate buffer cutting off the response.

What we did for closure:
- Replayed your curl requests 250x against the identical models and prompts (no failures observed).
- Inspected server logs for your session ids and the window you reported (no early termination events).
- Validated that model variants you listed returned expected token counts and no stop sequences were injected server-side.

Recommended next steps for FastRetail engineers (action items):
1) Run the same request without setting Content-Length and extend your client timeout to 30s; capture full response bytes and attach.
2) If using an SDK or proxy, temporarily bypass it and call the Redwood endpoint directly from a simple curl on a dev box.
3) If you use streaming, validate the chunk assembly logic — partial chunks displayed early can look like truncation.

We want to keep monitoring this. If you capture a raw truncated byte payload or can reproduce deterministically, please reopen the ticket and we'll escalate to infra for packet-level tracing and to the model team for deeper analysis.

As a courtesy for the time lost investigating, I've issued a one-time 5% credit on the account; details will appear in your billing portal. If you'd like, we can schedule a short pairing session with one of our SDK engineers to walk through captures.

Thanks again — and please let us know the results of the client-side runs.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
